title: Microscopic-Level Mouse Whole Cortex Simulation Composed of 9 Million Biophysical Neurons and 26 Billion Synapses on the Supercomputer Fugaku
problem: Understanding brain structure and function at cellular/synaptic level; simulating biophysical neural models at whole-cortex scale requires extreme computational resources
motivation: Building accurate digital replica of mammalian brain using publicly available anatomical and physiological data; validating HPC capabilities for extreme-scale neuroscience simulations
method: Lightweight biophysical neuron simulator optimized for Fugaku supercomputer; strong scaling benchmark up to 152,064 compute nodes; whole mouse cerebral cortex simulation on 145,728 Fugaku nodes
key_novelty: First demonstrated whole mammalian cortex biophysical simulation at scale; optimization and scaling of neuron simulator for exascale systems
contributions: Lightweight biophysical neuron simulator design optimized for Fugaku
Strong scaling demonstration: 7.13 petaflops at 152,064 nodes
Whole mouse cortex simulation: 9M neurons, 26B synapses on 145,728 nodes
Validation of HPC readiness for brain-scale simulations
limitations: Abstract lacks details on time-to-solution, I/O requirements, communication bottlenecks, or simulation accuracy metrics
